data.exact_reserve_text: The older years have seen reserve volatility during CY16 which has been explained in comments set out in the year of account review below; as to be expected there are no premium movements of any note on the run-off years 2012 and 2013 to offset these reserve deteriorations and the earning out of premiums in 2014 YOA has also been lower than the recalibration of ultimate reserve losses. Movement in the year comprises claims charges of GBP (2.5)m, additional reinsurance accruals of GBP (0.3)m, GBP (0.2)m of expense and provision charges and investment income of GBP 0.1m. Movement in 2016 comprises claims charges of GBP (5.0)m, GBP (0.4)m of additional reinsurance accruals, GBP 1.5m of expense and provision credits less charges, investment income of GBP 0.4m and GBP (1.3)m of exchange movements. unfavourable actual versus expected experience was noted in the review carried out for the six months ended 30 June 2016, which led to the to the development pattern and prior loss assumptions being revised and additional IBNR being booked.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a significant strengthening of prior year reserves in 2016, primarily driven by adverse claims development and IBNR recalibration across older years of account (2011-2014). Specific movements included claims charges for the 2012 and 2013 years of account due to unfavourable actual versus expected experience, leading to revisions in development patterns and additional IBNR. A late Contingency claim from 2015 also contributed to the strengthening, as did a large liability claim from a serious sporting accident in the 2013 year of account. The liability book, which includes casualty business, was particularly affected by this volatility.
